description:
## Background

The `opi-se9` decoder rewrite (PR #2) eliminated the per-delta O(n) spine walk and copy in `apply_delta` by storing `Message.Assistant.content` reverse-ordered internally and pattern-matching `[head | rest]` for the open block. Two related streaming costs were not addressed and warrant a follow-up.

## Cost #1 — Binary text accumulation (O(text²) per block)

Inside `apply_delta` for `text_delta` (and `thinking_delta`, `signature_delta`, `input_json_delta`), we still do:

```elixir
%{block | text: existing <> text}
```

Erlang's runtime can append-in-place to refc binaries only when exactly one reference to `existing` exists. `existing` is held by `state.message.content`'s head block, so the runtime allocates a new refc binary and copies on every delta. For a block of N bytes accumulated over m deltas, that's O(N²) bytes of binary churn, GC'd. Worst on long streamed responses (~50+ deltas per block).

Note: `input_json_delta` is special — it parses the accumulated string on every fragment via `PartialJson.parse_streaming/1`, so it must always have a flat binary. Iolist storage there would still need a flatten on every delta. Less of a win for that clause.

## Cost #2 — Spine reverse on every emit

Every emitted event carries `partial: present(message)` (decoder.ex:222), where `present/1` runs `:lists.reverse/1` on the content list. Per-emit cost is O(blocks). In practice blocks per response is ~1-3, so this is small in absolute terms but is a per-event constant factor.

## Why upstream pi-mono doesn't feel either cost

`pi-mono` (TS) carries the same `partial: AssistantMessage` field on every delta event (see `tmp/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/types.ts:251-258` — confirmed; we are contract-compatible). V8 gives them amortized O(1) `array.push` for the spine and ConsString ropes for binary concat — both deferred until inspection. BEAM has neither for free.

## Options identified

1. **Iolist storage for `block.text`, eager flatten in `present/1`** — contract-safe, asymptotically the same O(m²) total cost across the stream because flattens still happen on every emit. Better constant factor (one walk per emit vs one allocate-and-copy per delta) and much lower binary GC pressure. Low risk, modest win.

2. **Lazy `partial:` via thunk/accessor** — asymptotic win (per-emit becomes O(1) until consumer inspects). Breaks the upstream guarantee that `partial:` is a materialized `AssistantMessage` value. Acceptable if all consumers are inside octo_pi and we can change the contract; risky if we plan to port `pi-mom`, `pi-web-ui`, or anything else that consumes the upstream event shape.

3. **Drop `partial:` from delta events entirely** — biggest win, biggest deviation. Consumers reconstruct from `delta` if they want a snapshot, or call `Decoder.message/1`. Furthest from upstream; not recommended unless we're explicitly forking the contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- Profile a representative streaming response (~50-100 text_deltas across 1-3 blocks) on the current code. Capture: total binary allocations, GC count, wall time inside `apply_delta` and `present`.
- Decide which option (or none) based on measured impact.
- If implementing option (1): change `%Content.Text{text: …}` storage to allow iodata during streaming, flatten at `content_block_stop` (so closed blocks always carry binaries), and ensure `present/1` flattens any iodata before emit.
- If implementing option (2) or (3): write up the contract deviation and verify no current consumer breaks.

## Out of scope

Anything that would require a redesign of `Message.Assistant` external shape.
title: Revisit streaming partial: cost (binary churn + spine reverse on emit)
